newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL declines to comment on NZ retail talk.
newsitem.headline: FCL declines to comment on NZ retail talk.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Ltd spokesman Barry Akers on Wednesday declined to comment on speculation that Fletcher Energy may be about to become a player in the retail petrol market.
The New Zealand Herald earlier said New Zealand was expected to have another entrant to the market in competition with the so called "big four" international companies active here.
The paper said a company was believed to have bought up to 30 prime sites around the country for stations in a move that could potentially lead to cheaper prices at the pump.
The big four -- Mobil Corp, British Petroleum Co Plc, Shell and Caltex -- have been accused of widening their margins at the expense of competition.
Energy Minister Max Bradford said new competition would be "excellent news for consumers and the economy".

"The entry of new players into petrol retailing and distribution would provide the established oil majors with more incentive to seek and offer the best prices," Bradford said in a statement issued to the media during the day.

In a report earlier this year, the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research raised concerns about petrol pricing when it analysed price margins over the last decade. It suggested the gains made from deregulation had been lost over that period.
